methods.label: Sine maximum and its attainment
methods.explanation:
Assume, as in the recorded qualification, that \(\omega\ne0\) and the time domain contains a point where \(\sin(\omega t)=1\). The maximum value of sine is \(1\), so the highest temperature is \(10+8=18\).

The time-domain condition matters. For example, if \(\omega=1\) and \(\pi\le t\le2\pi\), then \(\sin t\le0\), with equality at the endpoints, so the highest temperature is \(10\). If the nonconstant assumption is also dropped, \(\omega=0\) gives the constant temperature \(10\).

Thus \(18\) is the intended answer under the recorded assumptions; without them, the highest temperature is not uniquely determined.
